newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus removes last missiles - Lukashenko aide.
newsitem.headline: Belarus removes last missiles - Lukashenko aide.

text.p: Belarus has returned to Russia the last batch of former Soviet strategic nuclear missiles deployed on its territory, a presidential aide told Reuters on Friday.

"The missiles have all gone," President Alexander Lukashenko's closest aide Vladimir Zametalin said, adding that they had been removed "recently" in line with the START-1 arms reduction treaty. Belarus was the last former Soviet republic to remove the missiles, following Ukraine and Kazakhstan.

Zametalin was speaking hours after Lukashenko and his parliamentary opponents reached a compromise -- mediated by Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin -- in a row over the president's plans to extend his powers by referendum.
Asked if the removal of the last of 72 SS-25 strategic missiles was connected to the referendum, Zametalin said: "It is possible to link everything to the referendum."
But diplomatic sources who asked not to be named told Reuters that the last missiles, controlled by Russian units, were transported to Russia for destruction on Thursday.

"We (Belarus) promised to ship all the nuclear missiles to Russia by the end of the year and we have fulfilled our promises," one Belarussian source said. "The last strategic missile was transferred yesterday."
